title: Consolidated RBAC v2 & SSO Audit: Threat Synthesis, Remediation Playbook, and Closure
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Synthesize findings from the Q1 security review, third-party pen-test, and internal threat modeling exercises across RBAC v2, SSO/SAML admin flows, and audit logging. Produce a single actionable remediation playbook with ownership, rollout plan, and verification steps so the security team can close outstanding findings and sign off on RBAC v2 for Dedicated & Private deployments.
acceptance_criteria: All high and critical pen-test findings related to RBAC v2, SAML SSO, and admin-privilged paths have documented mitigations or compensating controls
Audit logging gaps are identified, with at least one end-to-end test showing tamper-evident logs for admin events
SSO/SAML assertion handling hardening implemented for replay and signature validation edge cases
A canary rollout plan for RBAC rule migrations exists with automated rollback triggers and metrics
Security sign-off from AppSec and InfraSec documented in Confluence and linked to this ticket

notes: We observed two classes of issues from the pen test: policy-explosion leading to rule overlap, and a handful of SAML assertion replay and clock-skew validation edge-cases.

RBAC v2's policy evaluation path is optimized for speed; adding extra checks must be balanced with latency SLOs. Plan batched verification via background auditors rather than in-line checks where applicable.
Design trade-off: immutable log signing at write-time increases cost/latency; consider batching signatures per 1s window with sequence numbers to limit overhead.
Legal/compliance requested extended retention for admin audit trails; storage cost estimate attached in links.
decision_log: 2026-02-12: Decided to treat audit-log integrity as a separate pipeline responsibility (Observability) rather than adding complex crypto in the serving runtime.
2026-02-22: Agreed to adopt per-assertion nonce verification and strict clock-skew windows for SAML; non-zero skew will require explicit override documented and audited.
2026-03-01: Chosen canary strategy: 5% traffic for 48h, metric triggers for error-rate or policy-mismatch delta > 0.5%, automatic rollback to previous policy bundle.
remediation_plan: Short-term (P0): implement assertion nonce checks, tighten SAML signing verification, and patch the three critical endpoints identified by pen-test (ETA 2 weeks).
Medium-term (P1): add HMAC sequence to audit writes and a verifier service that replays signed windows to detect tampering (ETA 6 weeks).
Long-term (P2): RBAC policy linter + policy-sim tool to detect overlapping rules pre-deploy; integrate with CI and authoring console (ETA Q3).
Operational: update incident response playbooks and create dedicated alert for admin-privilege-rule-drift; SecOps to own runbook maintenance.
